mechanics.text: Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
assumptions: Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.

theme.text: A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
assumptions: Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.

environment.text: A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
assumptions: Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.

mechanics.text: Core loop: the player character stands within melee range of a single stationary target dummy and performs a punch action on player input (default binding: left mouse button or a designated 'Attack' button, e.g. E on keyboard / West face button on gamepad). Triggering the input plays a single punching animation on the player rig. Hit detection is resolved once per punch swing: a short-range forward hitbox/raycast is checked against the dummy's collider during the active frames of the punch animation. If the check registers contact with the dummy, exactly one 'hit' event fires: (1) a punch/impact sound effect plays, and (2) an on-screen hit counter increments by one. If the punch animation plays but does not connect with the dummy (player out of range or facing away), no sound plays and the counter does not increment. The dummy is immobile, has no health value, cannot be destroyed, and does not react beyond being the passive target of hit checks — it never resets, depletes, or triggers any secondary state. The counter is a simple persistent on-screen numeric display (e.g. 'Hits: 0') that only ever increases across the session; it is not a score, timer, combo multiplier, or damage value, and has no upper limit or reset condition. Input is rate-limited only by the natural duration of the punch animation (i.e., the player cannot start a new punch until the current animation finishes), preventing overlapping hit registrations from a single button press but adding no cooldown, combo, or stamina system beyond this animation-locking behavior.

Punch input default: left mouse click (PC) or a single mapped gamepad button; rebinding is out of scope unless requested later.
One dummy exists in the scene at a fixed position and orientation; it does not move, rotate, or respawn.
Hit detection uses a simple forward hitbox or short raycast from the player's fist/hand bone active only during the punch animation's strike frames.
Exactly one hit-and-counter increment can occur per completed punch animation cycle, even if the hitbox theoretically overlaps the dummy for multiple frames.
The punch/hit sound is a single audio clip with no variation, layering, or randomization requested.
The on-screen counter is a plain numeric text UI element with no styling, animation, or visual feedback beyond updating the number.
No cooldown, stamina, or resource system limits punching beyond the animation's own playback duration.
